rules.statement: No failure of a BEST_EFFORT listener changes the Outcome; a REQUIRED failure can only turn a Permit into 503.

rules.statement: A permit through a break-glass binding proceeds only when a REQUIRED listener recorded it; without one registered it is 503.
guards: runtime:BreakGlassAndShadowTest

rules.statement: A BEST_EFFORT event's hand-off never blocks or logs on the request's thread: a full or closed queue drops the event and counts it, and a reporter on the listeners' own dispatcher logs how many each listener dropped since its last line, at most once per warning interval, through a conflated signal (no unbounded hand-off).
guards: runtime:DecisionListenersShutdownTest#a full queue drops without waiting on the log, which is written off the request's thread

rules.statement: After a drain that timed out, or a cancel, no listener call starts: a call already running is not interrupted, every event still queued is dropped and counted, and an event offered as the listeners close is delivered or dropped, once, so delivered plus dropped is what was published.
guards: runtime:DecisionListenersShutdownTest#after a drain gives up, only the call in flight finishes and the queued events are dropped

runtime:DecisionListenersShutdownTest#an event offered after the listeners stopped is dropped and counted, not left queued
runtime:DecisionListenersShutdownTest#events published while the listeners drain are each delivered or dropped, once

rules.statement: With cosec-micrometer and a MeterRegistry, the data plane's snapshot source meters its cold, failed and timed-out loads (never a hit, which is every request's path), compiles, installs, evictions, regressions, lost documents, lag, refused hand-offs and refused housekeeping tasks under tags of closed value sets, never an app or tenant id; the documents it holds are reported by state as of its last lag pass and add up to what it holds; and a meter that fails never fails a load.
guards: micrometer:MicrometerSnapshotMetricsTest#the series are fixed, no event adds a meter
micrometer:MicrometerSnapshotMetricsTest#refused housekeeping tasks are counted by task
micrometer:MicrometerSnapshotMetricsTest#a hit is not metered

rules.source: RFC 0006 §9.5; usability review UD-7, UD-11 (maintainer's decisions, 2026-11-19)
rules.statement: Every output names what decided in the decision event's words (`outcome.reason`): the span as they are, the metrics' `result` in lower case, audit's `decision` in upper case, each through one exhaustive mapping. An explicit deny (`explicit_deny`, `EXPLICIT_DENY`) is only a request a DENY statement refused; a scope rejection, a boundary refusal and a `400` each have their own value, and a permit is `permit`/`PERMIT`. The event's `subject.method` is the credential's method as `CoSec-Identity` names it (`jwt`, `api-key`, or another verifier's name).
guards: runtime:AuditVocabularyTest#every reason has the audit decision of its own name
micrometer:ResultVocabularyTest#every reason has the result of its own name
runtime:SubjectMethodTest#the event names the credential as the identity header does

rules.statement: A service in gateway mode counts every refusal of a forwarded identity by problem type (`cosec.identity.refused{problem}`, whose values are the closed set of problems the gate answers, registered with cosec-micrometer and a MeterRegistry and kept without them), including those its log does not print, and logs the refusal's reason at WARN, at most once per interval for each problem type; the logged reason carries nothing of the header unescaped or unbounded (a control character or an unpaired surrogate as its `\uXXXX` escape, a name at most 64 characters, at most three names, a parse error by its location, never its text), and the response carries the problem only, never the reason.
guards: runtime:IdentityRefusalsTest#every refusal is counted by problem type, also those the bounded warning does not print
runtime:IdentityRefusalsTest#a request the gate lets through counts nothing, and no other problem is counted
runtime:IdentityRefusalsTest#the gate warns once for a flood of bad headers, and the response says only the problem
runtime:IdentityRefusalsTest#each problem type warns again once its interval has passed

document:IdentityCodecMessageTest#unknown members are escaped, bounded, and at most three are named
document:IdentityCodecMessageTest#text that is not JSON is named by where it fails, never by what it holds

rules.source: RFC 0007 §6.4; RFC 0006 §9.3 (design D2: saas-shadow-staged-design.md §4, §9 decisions 2 and 3, condition 3)
rules.statement: A BEST_EFFORT listener that reads only the events it sampled (the shadow listener) is offered only the events whose replay names it, and when every BEST_EFFORT listener is one and none samples a request, no decision event is made for that request. A REQUIRED listener, and every other BEST_EFFORT listener, receives every event whatever those sample. With cosec-micrometer and a MeterRegistry, `cosec.shadow.staged.age` is the time since this instance's store last answered its read of the staged list (NaN before the first answer), which keeps rising while the list cannot be read.
guards: runtime:SampledOnlyEventsTest#with only shadow listeners, a request none samples makes no event and a REQUIRED listener still gets it
runtime:SampledOnlyEventsTest#no event is made when only shadow listeners listen and none samples
runtime:SampledOnlyEventsTest#a request a shadow listener samples is offered to it

runtime:SampledOnlyEventsTest#each shadow listener is offered only the events it sampled
micrometer:ShadowStagedAgeMetricTest#the age is NaN before a read, zero after one, and rises while the list cannot be read

rules.source: Coordinator's brief, 2026-11-21 (one table for a cause's wire name, after #1792's control vocabulary); RFC 0006 §9.2
rules.statement: A decision's cause is named on the wire by one exhaustive table in cosec-runtime (`CauseName`), never by its class: the audit record's reason (`INDETERMINATE: <name>`), the shadow report's sample and the control API's `cause` write the same name for each kind of cause, a new kind does not compile until it is named, and the names stay the spellings 8.0's previews wrote.
guards: runtime:CauseNameTest#the table names every kind of cause, each by its pinned name
runtime:CauseNameTest#the audit record names each cause by its pinned name
runtime:CauseNameTest#the shadow sample names each cause by its pinned name
runtime:CauseNameTest#the audit record and the shadow sample never name a cause by its class

rules.source: Coordinator's brief for 8.0.0-beta.6, 2026-11-21 (the properties review, items 18 to 20); RFC 0006 §9.3, §7.1
rules.statement: A listener's two timeouts are derived, never set: a REQUIRED decision listener may take 20 % of `cosec.pipeline.timeout`, so its wait ends inside the request it delays; the REQUIRED change listeners of a control request together take `cosec.pipeline.timeout`, the bound of the request's own authorization, as no other deadline bounds a control request; at shutdown the decision listeners, the change listeners and the Kafka audit and change listeners each deliver what is queued for a sixth of `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase` (5 s at Spring's default 30 s). `cosec.observability.listener.required-timeout`, `cosec.observability.listener.drain-timeout` and `cosec.control.audit.required-timeout` fail startup as keys CoSec does not read, saying what replaced them.
guards: runtime:StageBudgetsTest#a required listener's wait ends inside the request
spring-boot:DerivedTimeoutsTest#without either deadline stated, every value is the default it replaced
spring-boot:StarterWiringTest#change listeners take the pipeline timeout as their required timeout and stop with the context
spring-boot:StarterWiringTest#the Kafka audit waits at shutdown for the listeners' drain timeout
spring-boot:SnapshotReadinessTest#listener queues are a share of the heap, and the drain a sixth of the shutdown phase

rules.source: Coordinator's brief for 8.0.0-beta.6, 2026-11-21 (the properties review, items 22, 23 and 26; memory by heap share); RFC 0006 §9.3
rules.statement: A BEST_EFFORT decision listener's queue holds its part of the decision listeners' share of the heap (`STA-12`), divided equally by the BEST_EFFORT listeners and counted in events at the measured size of an event of the pipeline's trace level (`HeapBudget.decisionEventBytes`: untraced, and traced at `full` and `exhaustive`, whose trace carries every candidate statement; each held by a test never below what such an event retains on a representative deployment's documents and at most twice it, the traced ones at their upper case, a denied request). A traced pipeline's queues hold fewer events, never the untraced count of traced events. The count is reckoned once, when the listeners are built: nothing is measured on the request path. A full queue drops the next event and counts it (`cosec.listener.dropped`).
guards: runtime:DecisionEventSizeTest#the constant a queue counts with is what a decision event retains at its trace level, within a factor of two
runtime:PipelineBuilderTest#a built pipeline's listener queues are one BEST_EFFORT listener's part of the heap share
spring-boot:SnapshotReadinessTest#listener queues are a share of the heap, and the drain a sixth of the shutdown phase
spring-boot:SnapshotReadinessTest#a traced pipeline's listener queues count events at their traced size

rules.source: RFC 0014 R1 on stored records and G5 (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24, after the red-team review CE-9, CE-10, CE-15); RFC 0014 §5 (sentences proposed in the PR); RFC 0014 G3
rules.statement: Every stored record the reader's rule refuses is counted by its kind of record and its reason (cosec.stored.refused{record, reason}), both closed sets: later for a record a later version wrote (a later format, or a member its crit names that this version does not know), malformed for one that is not a record of its kind. The count is kept per process, whichever store or caller read the record, and registered with cosec-micrometer and a MeterRegistry: a non-zero rate of later during a rolling upgrade is an instance still to upgrade, and ends when every instance runs the later version.
guards: micrometer:StoredRefusedMetricTest#each series reads the count of its record and reason, and the series are the closed sets only
document:StoredCritTest#a member crit names that this version does not know refuses the record as a later version's, and counts it
document:StoredCritTest#a crit that is not one, or a record that is not one, is malformed, and counts as malformed
